messages.content: free ai courses with building some stuff and not much codin g

Here’s a list of **free AI courses** that focus on **building cool stuff (projects)** and are **light on coding**, ideal if you want to grasp concepts and use tools with minimal programming:

---

## ✅ **1. Elements of AI (University of Helsinki)**
- **Website**: [elementsofai.com](https://www.elementsofai.com/)
- **Focus**: Intro to AI, real-world use cases, ethics.
- **Coding?** Very minimal — mostly theoretical and logical thinking.
- **Projects**: Conceptual applications, decision-making models.
- **Best for**: Beginners with zero to light coding skills.

---

## ✅ **2. Google's AI for Anyone (Kaggle Mini-Course)**
- **Website**: [Google AI for Anyone](https://www.cloudskillsboost.google/paths/118)
- **Focus**: AI basics, real-world tools like Teachable Machine, TensorFlow Lite.
- **Coding?** Almost none — mostly GUI-based tools.
- **Projects**: Image recognition, voice classification using visual tools.
- **Best for**: Hands-on learning without programming.

---

## ✅ **3. IBM AI Foundations for Everyone (Coursera)**
- **Website**: [Coursera: IBM AI Foundations](https://www.coursera.org/learn/ai-for-everyone)
- **Instructor**: IBM Skills Network
- **Coding?** None or optional.
- **Projects**: Basic business-level AI application planning.
- **Certificates**: Free with financial aid or audit mode.

---

## ✅ **4. Microsoft's AI School / AI Lab**
- **Website**: [https://aischool.microsoft.com](https://aischool.microsoft.com/)
- **Focus**: Real-world AI projects using Microsoft tools.
- **Coding?** Light to none in some beginner tracks.
- **Projects**: Face detection, language processing, translation tools.

---

## ✅ **5. Teachable Machine by Google**
- **Website**: [https://teachablemachine.withgoogle.com/](https://teachablemachine.withgoogle.com/)
- **Focus**: Train AI models using your webcam, voice, or images.
- **Coding?** None. Drag-and-drop model building.
- **Projects**: Real-time pose detection, sound classification, etc.
- **Fun Level**: Very high for beginners.

---

## ✅ **6. Fast.ai’s "Practical Deep Learning for Coders" (use AutoML tools)**
- **Website**: [https://course.fast.ai](https://course.fast.ai)
- **Coding?** Light coding with Jupyter notebooks, but focus on using high-level tools.
- **Projects**: Real deep learning projects like image classifiers.
- **Note**: Skip deeper code bits; just follow tutorials for project creation.

---

## Bonus: YouTube Playlists with Low-Code AI Projects

### 🎥 [CodeBasics: AI without coding](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLKnIA16_Rmvbr7zKYQuBfsVkjoLcJgxHH)
- Focuses on tools like Teachable Machine, Lobe AI, and Google AutoML.

### 🎥 [freeCodeCamp.org](https://www.youtube.com/c/Freecodecamp)
- Look for videos like "AI for Everyone", "How AI works", and beginner AI no-code tools.

---

### Want a recommendation based on your goal (e.g., face recognition app, text summarizer, etc.)?
Just tell me — I can give you the **most practical, no-code/low-code course** or tool for that.

Here are **top free websites** where you can find **full AI courses** (project-based or practical-focused) — and some have **certificates** too. All of these are **100% free**, not just trial versions.

---

## 🧠 1. [**Kaggle Learn**](https://www.kaggle.com/learn/overview)
### ✅ What’s Good:
- Mini-courses (10–20 lessons)
- Uses **interactive Jupyter Notebooks**
- Hands-on, not too much coding
- Good for building real AI/ML projects like:
  - Titanic survival predictor
  - House price prediction
  - NLP basics

---

## 🧠 2. [**Google AI / Learn with Google AI**](https://ai.google/education/)
### ✅ What’s Good:
- Beginner to advanced
- No-code tools: Teachable Machine, AutoML
- Hands-on AI experiments
- Real use-case demos (face detection, speech, etc.)

---

## 🧠 3. [**Fast.ai**](https://course.fast.ai/)
### ✅ What’s Good:
- Full deep learning course
- Practical-first (start building AI early)
- Minimal code at the start (focus on results)
- Projects like:
  - Image classifier
  - Text generator
  - Object detector

---

## 🧠 4. [**Microsoft Learn – AI Track**](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/paths/introduction-artificial-intelligence/)
### ✅ What’s Good:
- Full structured learning paths
- Covers AI concepts and real-world apps
- Some modules use **low-code tools** (Azure, Power Platform)
- Certification of completion (free MS Learn account needed)

---

## 🧠 5. [**Harvard's CS50: Introduction to AI with Python**](https://cs50.harvard.edu/ai/)
### ✅ What’s Good:
- Fully free
- Project-based (e.g., search, games, machine learning)
- Requires **some coding**, but structured step-by-step
- Includes video lectures + assignments

---

## 🧠 6. [**Coursera (Audit Mode)**](https://www.coursera.org/)
- Search **"AI for Everyone" by Andrew Ng** or **"AI Foundations by IBM"**
- Enroll in **audit mode** to get full course access **for free**
- No certificate unless you pay, but you get:
  - All videos
  - All assignments
  - All quizzes

---

## 🧠 7. [**MIT OpenCourseWare – Artificial Intelligence**](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/electrical-engineering-and-computer-science/6-034-artificial-intelligence-fall-2010/)
### ✅ What’s Good:
- Entire course materials free
- Lectures, assignments, and exams included
- Very academic and in-depth
- Needs coding knowledge (Python)

---

### 👶 Want Almost **No Coding**?

Try these:

- [Teachable Machine](https://teachablemachine.withgoogle.com/) (build AI models using webcam or voice — no code)
- [Lobe.ai](https://www.lobe.ai/) (Microsoft's no-code model trainer)
- [RunwayML](https://runwayml.com/) (AI video/image editing, no code, used in real production work)

---
